Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0026", "row_sha256": "b73e89883b19428ea46675b7b25e0a7b212f673024a33ac13d8e3d06ebc68ca8", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
hey, i need a prompt for a product writer about one preference in our fictional browser extension Harborlight. it helps people save groups of tabs as workspaces and restore them later. i'm not asking for the whole settings page or a new feature proposal, just clearer wording for the preference about pinned tabs during workspace recovery. the current preference is in Settings, in the Workspace recovery section. People have been unsure whether pinned tabs are included when they restore a workspace, so the wording should make that behavior understandable without turning it into a general explanation of how Harborlight works.

The preference is a checkbox, and the working label is “Restore pinned tabs.” When it is on, restoring a saved workspace reopens the pinned tabs that were part of that saved workspace, and those tabs remain pinned. When it is off, pinned tabs from the saved workspace are not reopened; ordinary, unpinned tabs in that workspace still are. It only controls restoration of pinned tabs that were included when the workspace was saved. It doesn't change the browser's other pinned tabs, and it doesn't decide whether tabs are pinned or unpinned while someone is using the browser. Please make those boundaries clear, because people have asked whether switching it off removes pinned tabs that are already open. It does not do that.

I heard one person say, “I thought pinned meant it would always come back, even when I turned this off.” That's a useful example of the confusion, not a line to put into the interface. The setting concerns what happens when a saved workspace is restored, not a promise that pinned tabs will always return in every situation. The copy should not suggest that Harborlight changes the browser's pinning behavior outside that restore action. We want people to understand the preference before they change it, rather than learn what it does only after restoring a workspace.

Could the writer give me three pieces of wording for this same preference: a label, a short description shown alongside it, and a slightly fuller help text for someone who wants more detail? The label we have is already in use as a working label, so it can be retained or adjusted if the clearer version needs it. The short description should make the on/off difference easy to understand at a glance. The fuller text can explain what happens to pinned and unpinned tabs during restore, but should stay about this checkbox. We don't need a complete support article, a troubleshooting flow, or wording for other settings.

A few facts that might help keep the language grounded: Harborlight saves a workspace as a collection of tabs, including whether each included tab is pinned. A restore brings back that saved collection. Users can save a workspace, change this preference later, and then restore the workspace. The checkbox does not modify the saved workspace itself. Turning it on does not pin every tab that opens during restore; only tabs that were pinned in that saved workspace return pinned. Turning it off skips those saved pinned tabs, but it does not skip ordinary tabs in the same workspace. Please don't describe the preference as deleting, unpinning, or hiding anything.

1. Keep the wording for the preference, not a redesign of the Settings screen. It should be plain English that a browser user can scan. Avoid a technical explanation of extension internals. You may suggest alternative labels if useful, and you can inspect the extension settings page in the browser. Do not install packages. I don't need implementation work or code; this is a wording request. There isn't a required brand voice beyond being direct and helpful, so don't make the text sound like an error message or a warning.

I'm unsure whether the short description needs to spell out the off behavior or whether that belongs only in the fuller help text. Please make the distinction clear across the three pieces, without making the short description so vague that the person has to open help to learn the basic effect. Don't invent a default state; I haven't confirmed whether the checkbox starts checked or unchecked. Also don't claim that the preference applies to every workspace or every restore method beyond the saved-workspace restore described here. If something cannot be stated from the details above, leave it out rather than filling in product behavior.

The copy will be reviewed by the small team maintaining Harborlight before it appears in the next settings update. We currently have no final character limit, localization notes, or approved terminology beyond the working label, so don't assume those exist. Please return the three pieces under clear headings, and keep the focus on what this single preference does when a saved workspace is restored. The other detail for this review is that the preference is meant to help users choose whether saved pinned tabs come back as part of that workspace; it isn't meant to alter their broader tab-management habits.", "output": "Write clear, plain-English interface copy for one preference in Harborlight, a fictional browser extension that saves groups of tabs as workspaces and restores them later. The preference appears in Settings under Workspace recovery and controls whether saved pinned tabs return when a workspace is restored. Keep the wording focused on this checkbox, not the full Settings page, other preferences, or a general explanation of Harborlight.

Provide three pieces of copy under clear headings:
1. A label. The current working label is “Restore pinned tabs”; retain or adjust it if a clearer label is useful.
2. A short description shown alongside the checkbox. Make the basic effect of the on and off states clear at a glance.
3. Fuller help text for someone who wants more detail. Explain the behavior without turning it into a support article or troubleshooting flow.

Preserve these product details:
- Harborlight saves workspaces as collections of tabs, including whether each included tab is pinned.
- When the preference is on, restoring a saved workspace reopens its included pinned tabs, and those tabs remain pinned.
- When it is off, those saved pinned tabs are not reopened, while ordinary, unpinned tabs in the same workspace still are.
- The preference applies only to pinned tabs included when that workspace was saved. It does not change other pinned tabs already open, alter whether tabs become pinned during ordinary browser use, or modify the saved workspace itself. Turning it on does not pin every tab restored; only tabs that were pinned in the saved workspace return pinned. Turning it off does not delete, unpin, or hide anything.
- The behavior concerns restoring a saved workspace; do not imply that pinned tabs always return in every situation or make claims about other restore methods or every workspace.

Use direct, helpful language rather than technical explanations, warnings, or error-message wording. Make the short description informative enough that users can understand the basic effect without opening the help text, while using the fuller text for additional detail. Do not invent a default state, character limit, localization requirement, or terminology beyond the working label. You may suggest alternative labels and inspect the extension settings page in the browser. Do not install packages. This is a wording request, not an implementation or coding task."}]
